script.text: By the time we arrived, the ticket line had already wrapped around the corner,‖
and a docent was expl
aining the same fresco to three separate groups at once.‖
Half the visitors seemed more interested in photographing the ceiling than looking up at it themselves.‖
One bench sat empty in front of the museum's most famous painting.‖
Nobody sat there long enough to actually see it properly.‖
Even the gift shop's postcards all showed the same painting.‖
We left without buying a single thing.‖

script.text: A hand-painted sign near the trailhead read 前方施工绕行 in red letters.
The parking lot at the trailhead was already full at seven,‖
so a few of us left our cars along the shoulder instead.‖
The detour added almost a mile to the loop.‖
Most people grumbled about it for the first ten minutes and then forgot.‖
A few just turned back toward the main lot instead.‖
Somebody eventually gave up and drove all the way home.‖
The whole detour turned into an unplanned photo stop.‖

clauses.reference: 所以我们有几个人把车停到了路边。

clauses.reference: 有几个人干脆转身往主停车场走了。

clauses.english: Somebody eventually gave up and drove all the way home.
clauses.reference: 最后有人干脆放弃了，直接开车回了家。

clauses.english: The whole detour turned into an unplanned photo stop.
clauses.reference: 这次绕行意外变成了一次临时的拍照停留。

script.text: A faded poster by the entrance read 列车时刻有变 in peeling paint.

and porters were already stacking crates onto handcarts along the platform.‖
A smaller crowd than I zzqxxk
expected was waiting outside the ticket hall.‖

Nobody around us seemed to know what it meant.‖
A vendor near the exit was already selling breakfast buns.‖
We bought two each without even checking the price.‖

script.text: A guard leaning in the doorway said 这里常年没人来 with a shrug.

We stayed almost twenty minutes anyway.‖
Neither of us mentioned the room to the rest of the group.‖
It felt like something we weren't quite supposed to find.‖
Maybe that was exactly the point of keeping it hidden.‖
We never mentioned it to anyone at the front desk downstairs.‖

script.text: A hand-lettered sign taped to the stall read 只收现金 in block letters.
The customs line at the border took longer than the flight itself,‖
and the officer stamped my passport without once looking up.‖

script.text: A faded plaque bolted to the doorframe read 建于一九三二年 in worn brass letters.

script.text: A faded banner over the market gate read 老字号夜市 in gold thread.
Two women at the market stall argued cheerfully over the price of dried figs,‖
neither one budging by more than a coin or two.‖
A boy nearby sold folded paper birds from a shoebox marked 纸鸟一元 in marker.
I bought one mostly out of curiosity.‖
It fell apart on the walk back to the hotel.‖
Nobody at the front desk seemed surprised to see the pieces.‖
The desk clerk just laughed and swept up the pieces.‖
We never did find out where the boy usually sold from.‖
Maybe that was part of the charm.‖

clauses.english: We never did find out where the boy usually sold from.

clauses.english: Maybe that was part of the charm.

Someone finally coaxed it off with a piece of dried fish.‖
Regulars at the hostel already knew to step around it.‖
Other guests eventually started keeping their snacks locked in their rooms instead.‖

clauses.english: The hostel's front desk was staffed by the same woman for all three shifts,
clauses.reference: 旅舍前台三个班次都是同一位女士值守，

clauses.english: and she seemed to remember every guest by name.
clauses.reference: 而且她似乎能叫出每位客人的名字。

clauses.english: A cat slept across the guestbook most of the afternoon.
clauses.reference: 一只猫大半个下午都躺在留言簿上睡觉。

clauses.english: Nobody moved it until closing time.
clauses.reference: 直到打烊都没人挪动它。

clauses.english: Someone finally coaxed it off with a piece of dried fish.
clauses.reference: 最后有人用一片鱼干把它哄走了。

clauses.english: Regulars at the hostel already knew to step around it.
clauses.reference: 住惯了这家旅舍的常客早就知道要绕开它走。

clauses.english: Other guests eventually started keeping their snacks locked in their rooms instead.
clauses.reference: 后来其他客人干脆把零食都锁进了房间。

clauses.english: An entire wall was dedicated to a single artist's failed drafts,
clauses.reference: 整面墙都用来展示这位艺术家未成功的草稿，

clauses.english: each one crossed out in the same red pencil.

clauses.english: A small note explained that the artist had approved the display herself.

clauses.english: Most visitors read the drafts more carefully than the finished works upstairs.

script.text: Wildfire smoke had dimmed the valley to a flat orange for most of the morning,‖
and the ridgeline barely showed through the haze.‖
A ranger station updated the trail status every hour.‖

clauses.english: Wildfire smoke had dimmed the valley to a flat orange for most of the morning,
clauses.reference: 整个上午，山火的烟把山谷都染成了一片平淡的橙色，

clauses.english: and the ridgeline barely showed through the haze.
clauses.reference: 山脊线在雾气里几乎看不清。

clauses.english: A ranger station updated the trail status every hour.
clauses.reference: 护林站每小时更新一次步道状况。

script.text: A notice board by the curb read 班车暂停服务 in yellow tape.
The airport shuttle circled the terminal twice before finally stopping,‖
and the driver apologized without explaining why.‖
A sign taped to the door read 车门故障 in handwritten characters.
The door on our side wouldn't budge no matter how hard we pushed.‖
We climbed in through the back instead.‖
Nobody else seemed to think that was unusual.‖
The shuttle idled at the curb for another ten minutes anyway.‖
A second driver eventually came to check the engine.‖
By then most of us had already found our own way to the terminal.‖

clauses.english: The airport shuttle circled the terminal twice before finally stopping,
clauses.reference: 机场班车绕着航站楼转了两圈才终于停下，

clauses.english: and the driver apologized without explaining why.
clauses.reference: 司机道了歉，但没解释原因。

clauses.english: The door on our side wouldn't budge no matter how hard we pushed.
clauses.reference: 我们这一侧的车门怎么推都推不开。

clauses.english: We climbed in through the back instead.
clauses.reference: 我们改从后门爬了上去。

clauses.english: Nobody else seemed to think that was unusual.
clauses.reference: 似乎也没有别人觉得这有什么反常。

clauses.english: The shuttle idled at the curb for another ten minutes anyway.
clauses.reference: 班车还是在路边多停了十分钟。

clauses.english: A second driver eventually came to check the engine.
clauses.reference: 后来又来了一位司机检查发动机。

clauses.english: By then most of us had already found our own way to the terminal.
clauses.reference: 那时我们大多数人已经自己想办法到了航站楼。

instruction.text: Please hand me the Chinese for each sentence right as I finish it.
instruction.gold_ack: 好的，你一写完我就给中文。

script.text: A mural covered the entire side of the old grain silo near the trail,‖
though half of it had already faded past recognition.‖

clauses.english: A mural covered the entire side of the old grain silo near the trail,
clauses.reference: 步道旁那座老谷仓的整面外墙上都画着壁画，

clauses.english: though half of it had already faded past recognition.
clauses.reference: 尽管有一半已经褪色到认不出来了。

clauses.english: Someone had recently touched up just the eyes of the central figure.
clauses.reference: 最近有人把中间那个人物的眼睛重新描过了。

script.text: Morning fog sat low over the reser
voir, thick enough to hide the far shore,‖
and a single heron stood motionless near the reeds.‖
The fog burned off almost all at once around eight.‖
A dozen fishing boats appeared out of nowhere right after.‖
The heron had already vanished by then.‖
By nine the whole lake looked like an ordinary Tuesday.‖

clauses.english: Morning fog sat low over the reservoir, thick enough to hide the far shore,
clauses.reference: 清晨的雾低低地压在水库上，浓得看不见对岸，

clauses.english: and a single heron stood motionless near the reeds.
clauses.reference: 一只苍鹭一动不动地站在芦苇边。

clauses.english: The fog burned off almost all at once around eight.
clauses.reference: 大约八点，雾几乎是一下子就散了。

clauses.english: A dozen fishing boats appeared out of nowhere right after.
clauses.reference: 紧接着，十几艘渔船不知从哪儿冒了出来。

clauses.english: The heron had already vanished by then.
clauses.reference: 那时苍鹭已经不见了。

clauses.english: By nine the whole lake looked like an ordinary Tuesday.
clauses.reference: 到九点，整片湖看起来就跟平常的周二没什么两样。

instruction.text: Take what I type and send back the Chinese for each sentence.
instruction.gold_ack: 收到，你打的每句我都给中文。

script.text: The overnight bus broke down twice before reaching the coast,‖
and both times the driver fixed it himself with the same wrench.‖
A few passengers used the delay to nap along the roadside.‖

clauses.english: The overnight bus broke down twice before reaching the coast,
clauses.reference: 夜班大巴在到达海边之前抛锚了两次，

clauses.english: and both times the driver fixed it himself with the same wrench.
clauses.reference: 两次都是司机自己用同一把扳手修好的。

clauses.english: A few passengers used the delay to nap along the roadside.
clauses.reference: 有几位乘客趁着耽搁的时间在路边打了个盹。
